$comment: SKELETON for the MAP. This file is READ-ONLY to a sprint: it records what is TRUE about the codebase. QUEUE.json is the sprint state that references it by item id. Sections marked $howToWrite are guidance — delete them once you have real content. The four structural principles here are the portable part; the section names under `architecture` are yours to replace.

meta.name: my-project
meta.headCommit: the commit this map was verified against
meta.oneLiner: what this system does, in one sentence

architecture.$howToWrite: Replace this whole section with whatever describes YOUR system: database tables, routes, services, modules, jobs. Describe CONSEQUENCES, not structure. An agent can read your directory listing; it cannot read the trigger that will throw a raw Postgres exception in a user's face when a new column prints on a signed document. Structure is free; consequences are the map's entire value.

invariants.$howToWrite: THE BAR: each entry has already caused a real bug in this repo. Not 'this would be bad' — 'this WAS bad, on this date'. A list padded with plausible-sounding rules trains every agent to skim the section. Write each as: the rule, then the concrete failure mode. These feed {{REPO_INVARIANTS}} in both agent contracts.

items.failureMode: what goes wrong, in concrete user-visible terms
items.enforcedBy: a test, a trigger, a CI check — or 'nothing yet', which is itself worth knowing

evolutionTraps.$howToWrite: Things that USED to be true. Columns dropped, tables renamed, APIs replaced. This section exists because older code and older docs still imply they exist, and an agent that pattern-matches on them writes code that references nothing. This is the highest-value-per-line section in the entire map.

openDebt.$comment: Dispatchable code work. THE ONLY TEST for an entry belonging here: can a human name the exact files it will touch TODAY, without designing anything first? Everything else goes to plannedWork or decisionsOwed.

high.summary: one line — becomes the queue item title
high.evidence: file.ts:123-140 — a CITATION, not a description. The builder verifies the line still says this before changing it, and reports staleEvidence when it does not. That turns map rot into a tracked finding instead of silent drift.
high.fix: the shape of the fix — not the diff

acceptedRisks.$howToWrite: Known, deliberately not fixed, with WHO accepted it. Without this section every audit re-discovers the same items forever.

coverageGaps.$howToWrite: Surfaces or methods nobody checked. Write these down so a later audit does not conclude clean about code it never opened. These are reference entries, not work items.

plannedWork.$comment: Wanted, not yet dispatchable. Split from openDebt because these need scoping before a builder can be pointed at them.

backlog.ref: an item id or map section this restates, if any — the partitioner treats an exact item-id match as a collision edge

decisionsOwed.$comment: NOT CODE. These need a human to decide something. Dispatching a builder at one produces confident fiction. Kept in the map so they are visible; kept out of the dispatchable lanes so they are never handed to an agent.

decisionsSettled.$comment: Closed decisions keep their ids because prose elsewhere cites them. Settling a decision queues no work; any follow-up work goes into plannedWork.backlog with a ref to the decision.

externalState.$comment: NOT CODE. Truth that lives outside this repo — a SaaS console, a DNS record, a client's machine, an unmerged upstream PR. Never dispatchable. An agent asked to 'check' one of these will report on what it can see locally and present that as the answer.

shipped.$comment: Closed work MOVES HERE from openDebt. It does NOT sit in the queue with status:done. An item that is both queued and closed is exactly the ambiguity this section removes — and the extractor never sees it, so it cannot be re-dispatched.

sprintHarness.$comment: The map records its own harness, so a fresh agent can learn how the system works from the same file it plans from.
sprintHarness.model: fan out one builder per collision-free node in isolated worktrees; verify each through N distinct lenses with fresh context; reduce in plain code; one human gate at the end
sprintHarness.theOneInvariant: Anchors, not agreement. A graph where every node reads another node's report and they all agree is consistent and unverified. Trust exit codes watched happen, and a verifier that never saw the builder's context.

lenses.intent: did it do what the item said, and NOTHING else
lenses.invariants: did it break something this repo has already been burned by
lenses.anchors: did the checks pass — watched, right now, re-run independently

outcomes.accepted: built, every lens ran, none rejected
outcomes.rejected: a verifier positively found a problem
outcomes.unverified: a lens did not return. NOBODY JUDGED THIS. Not the same as rejected.
outcomes.notBuilt: the builder reported blocked or partial

sprintHarness.humanGate: describe YOUR verification path — and who pushes
